info.title: KNX IoT 3rd Party API
info.description: This KNX IoT 3rd Party API offers an access at the level of the Installation and supports more sophisticated queries to (history) values of installation state data or specific elements of the installation, such as location, application function and datapoints.

get.description: List all available information of a specific subscription.  NA.          With this access method you cannot: -  retrieve all to a subscription belonging (previously upon subscribed) resource items   A full list of the actual datapoints belonging to a subscription is resolvable via the endpoint subscription/{id}/datapoints.  ## Implementation Details In case no specific information will be available as part of the JSON API `relationships`,  `meta` or `attributes` member, the member MUST NOT be expressed. ### Attributes - KNX vendor specific attributes MUST be expressed with its (predefined) corresponding namespace.   - Not in this API specified attributes from the KNX information model SHOULD be expressed    with its corresponding data property name from the KNX information model.  ### Relationships - Only for this API specified `relationships` member can be expressed.  - KNX vendor specific relationships or not in this API specified relationships    from the KNX information model MUST not be expressed and if any ignored.  Examples, see **Runtime** example on status code 200.

parameters.name: subscriptionId
parameters.description: The id from requested subscription.

parameters.name: mac
parameters.description: The MAC address of the controller on which the operation is to be performed. This controller must be owned or shared with the user performing the request. If the mac address is not set, the user's active controller is used.

200.description: The response with message data containing of (JSON API) member: - `data` member -> subscription item, including:   - id/ type   - an `attributes` member describing the subscription properties (url, secret, caCert)   - an `meta` member describing the _subscription type_   - a (single) `relationships` member, describing a link to an endpoint providing all datapoints of this subscription  For security reasons it is **strongly** recommended to NOT include the (optional)  subscription properties (part of `attributes` and `meta` members) in the response when you operate in public environments.  In a local environment the attributes may be included in the response (such as for debug reasons).  The current AN198 deviates from this payload definition, this will be updated in the next version of the AN.  In this YAML file it is specified as follows:    - individual subscription items with its id/ subscription resource type (such as room, datapoint, ...) are    not included in the response payload (see Notes above)

put.description: An individual subscription will be updated on the server.  It must be ensured that updated/overwritten elements do not impact the current operational state. - url - secret   - caCert (may be expired)   With this access method you cannot: - add new (to be subscribed upon) resource items to the existing subscription - overwrite the current subscription type (the subscription characteristics)    A full reconfiguration of an (individual) subscription is only possible with  the deletion of the current subscription and re-creation of a new subscription.

get.description: List all available locations of the installation, this includes also all root locations.  It is possible to limit the number of returned items.  Additionally also to skip collection items before reading. - Location with type "room": it is possible to change the title attribute and the parent location. The parent location must be of type "floor".

post.description: An individual subscription will be created at the server, as a result a subscription **id** is generated that belongs to all involved datapoints.   The subscription **request** contains: 1. the resource items to be subscribed upon (which is an datapoint directly or an resource that contains datapoints) 2. the _subscription type_  (the characteristics of the subscription) 3. the callback URL, shared secret and optional certificate  The _subscription type_ from point 2 above supports two characteristics on a CoV for a datapoint.: 1. include subordinated resources for a CoV 2. include no subordinated resources for a CoV   The request body allows to bundle an array of resource items with its possibly **different**  individual resource types (such as room, device or datapoint).  A _subscription type_ specified with the subordinated characteristics (point 1) will only affect  resources of type location. On other resources this _subscription type_ will be handled from the  server as in point 2.

The latter is part of the `datapointSubscription` member.   As a note, the subscription <id> MUST be unique for all resource items,  that need to be subscribed and are part of an individual subscription request.

parameters.description: The number of items to return.

200.description: The response with event data consisting of (JSON API) members: - `meta` member > collection information - `data` member > collection of responses, each including:   - id/ type   - some response attributes    - some links to     - an endpoint providing the same data     - an endpoint providing the parent data

get.summary: Get version and entry point information.
get.description: Get information on the supported API versions from this node. Additionally, how to access  the installation root entry points.  The endpoint MUST not secured with any authorization or token. It is used to discover the API server.     Implementation Details - The URL MUST not contain any API base path element.  - The version member value MUST contain only a major and minor number according    to the format major.minor, represented as a string.  - The major number starts from value 1, the minor number starts with value 0. - The version element does not follow the JSON API version element (version : {api:2.0})

200.description: The response with message data containing of (JSON) member: - `api` member > most recent supported API version item, including version/ base path URL - `supportedversions` member > additionally supported (older) API version items, each including version/ base path URL - some `links`member, collection of useful (free to define) relations such as the /installations or /node endpoint,   each item including   - link   - description   - content type

Errors.description: Array of error items, included in the JSON API `errors` member.  Each error item must be conform to RFC 7807. It may contain additional information such as:  - a JSON API `links` member, pointing to absolute/ relative URL with error details   - a vendor specific information

title.description: Error title or HTTP status phrase.

links.description: Absolute URL reference to a detailed description of the error.

SubscriptionUpdate.description: Subscription message data, containing of (JSON API) member: - `data` member -> subscription item, including:    - id/ type   - an `attributes` member describing the subscription properties (url, secret, caCert)  The current AN198 deviates from this payload definition, this will be updated in the next version of the AN.  In this YAML file it is specified as follows:  - individual subscription items with its id/ subscription resource type (such as room, datapoint, ...) are    not included in the request payload (see Notes above) - meta member, describing the subscription type (the subscription characteristics) is not included        For the handling of not present elements in  the request body, see <https://jsonapi.org/format/#crud-updating-resource-attributes>
